rows.what the ink shows: The deletion leaves a left-facing head and a right-facing head visible. Between them the shaft is a broad filled blue band intersected by the long cancellation stroke; at 5x its putative two horizontal strokes are not separately recoverable. The bidirectional sign is supported, but the exact doubled-shaft form remains uncertain.

Below the long deletion stroke, a low curved e entry rises toward a tall t stem. The stem descends below the word baseline and has a short rightward crossbar distinct from the longer cancellation strokes. These surviving e-plus-t strokes support et despite the crossing ink.

Inside the parentheses, the compressed first word has a long low run with a small central upward stroke and two taller ending strokes. The second word begins with the tall narrow downstroke and low hook of f, followed by a dot, a low connecting run and a second raised dot before the small final stroke. There is no lower closed b bowl or acute accent supporting bornées; the visible dotted sequence supports finies.

After Nous ne nous, the word starts with a short rising s stroke and a low horizontal e run. The middle connected strokes have a small rise then a downturned v ending; a separate dot sits over the following short i stroke. A long low terminal run ends with a small downward hook before pas. This compressed sequence supports servirons.
